lines.text: Every building has one person who knows it by heart.
By 2036, 12.9 million people in Germany reach retirement age.
Gisela is new here. Nobody told her which bracket is loose.
Forty-two percent of what a company knows lives only in individual people's heads. When they leave, the money walks out with them.
Today's tools list what to check. None of them walks you there. None remembers what you found.
Meet Wanda: Google Maps for the inside of your building.
She plans her round on the laptop. Then she just talks to it, like to a colleague.
Every note lands in the building's knowledge graph: who, where, when, with a photo. It stays, even when people retire.
Behind the easy talk, every fact comes from code: routes, rounds, doors. The AI only listens and speaks.
Every answer is computed, so every answer can be checked.
It works on any building, even from the evacuation plan on the wall.
The knowledge stays in the building.
